g.title: MAH_QSP_Model
g.text: Hypercalcaemia of Malignancy — QSP Mechanistic Map
Plasma calcium is not a stock but the RESIDUAL of three fluxes on three clocks — bone (days), gut (a day), kidney (hours) — and no single drug moves more than one of them fast.

The renal escape valve has a CEILING that is itself a function of the calcium it is excreting: hypercalcaemia causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, nausea and vomiting, which contract the ECF, which drops GFR, which lowers the ceiling.

When bone resorption exceeds that ceiling no steady state exists — the crisis is a saddle-node, not a big number. Saline is fast because it raises the ceiling; bisphosphonate is slow because it is delivered by the very process it stops.

g.title: X_why
g.text: WHY NO DRUG IS BOTH FAST AND DEFINITIVE
Saline works in hours because it acts on clock 1,
and for the same reason it cannot cure anything.
Bisphosphonate is definitive because it acts on clock 3,
and for the same reason it cannot rescue today.
The guideline combination is not additive chemistry —
it is a RELAY between two clocks.
